article_blocks.text: Strain Type: 60% Sativa / 40% Indica
Genetics: Yumbolt × G13 Haze
Breeder: Resin Seeds
THC Content: 19–23%
CBD Content: N/A
Terpene Profile: N/A
Primary Flavors: Sweet fruit, berry, citrus, spice, herbs
Flowering Time (Indoor): 9–10 weeks
Outdoor Harvest Time: September to October
Indoor Yield: 400 g/m²
Outdoor Yield: 150–300 g per plant
Grow Difficulty: Intermediate

Yummy is a strain whose uncomplicated name hides a surprisingly serious genetic background. Resin Seeds created the cultivar by taking a particularly desirable Yumbolt female selected in 2003 and crossing it with a G13 Haze male, bringing together old Humboldt-influenced sweetness with one of the classic G13/Haze combinations. Instead of pushing the hybrid toward the candy-and-cream style common in newer marijuana strains , the breeder focused on a more traditional contrast: deep sweetness and relaxing physical character from Yumbolt balanced by spice, cerebral lift, and the gradual “creeper” quality of G13 Haze. Resin Seeds ultimately classified the finished line as 60% sativa and 40% indica, with THC ranging from approximately 19–23%.

Its personality comes from the way those two parents interact rather than from one overwhelming trait. The aroma can begin with sweet fruit and berry before moving toward citrus, dry spice, herbs, wood, and Haze-like depth. Effects follow a similarly staged pattern. Relaxation can appear early, but the mental side continues building after the first few minutes, producing a high that may feel considerably stronger once the delayed G13 Haze influence is fully established. Yummy consequently occupies an interesting middle ground: approachable enough to remain balanced, yet complex enough in flavor and effect to appeal to experienced cannabis consumers who enjoy older-school hybrid genetics.
Genetics and Lineage

Resin Seeds identifies the direct cross as Yumbolt × G13 Haze and provides an important detail about the maternal side: the Yumbolt used in the project was a special plant selected in 2003. The breeder wanted to retain that plant’s sweetness and relaxing qualities while introducing additional spice and a slower-building cerebral effect from G13 Haze. This was therefore not simply a generic crossing of whatever Yumbolt and Haze plants happened to be available; the selection of the Yumbolt female was central to the project.

Yumbolt itself was created by Sagarmatha Seeds from old Humboldt County material. Sagarmatha describes the line as having roots believed to trace back to Afghan genetics that became established in Humboldt County, California, during the late 1970s. It became particularly famous for exceptionally sweet flavor, dense frosted flowers, and a comfortable, dreamy stone. Yumbolt also won first place in the Seeds Indica category at the 2001 High Times Cannabis Cup , giving the maternal side of Yummy an established competition pedigree.

G13 Haze contributes a very different genetic direction. Mr. Nice Seedbank identifies its classic G13 Haze as G13 × Haze , combining a predominantly Afghan-derived G13 side with an inbred Haze family . The parent is valued for potency, flavor, and strong hybrid-breeding potential, while its Haze ancestry introduces longer-lasting cerebral intensity and aromatic spice. Bringing that male to Yumbolt created a cultivar in which Afghan-influenced sweetness and body relaxation meet the brighter, more expansive qualities of classic Haze.
Effects and Experience

The effect develops in stages rather than arriving all at once. Yumbolt contributes a comfortable physical ease that can make the first part of the experience feel deceptively gentle. Mood softens, the body becomes less tense, and music, conversation, food, or low-pressure activities can become more enjoyable without an immediate sense of mental overload. Resin Seeds specifically highlights the relaxing character inherited from Yumbolt.

G13 Haze changes the experience as time passes. The breeder describes the high as having a creeping quality, meaning its full strength may not be obvious immediately after consumption. Mental activity can gradually become more pronounced, with thoughts becoming more associative, sensory details more interesting, and the overall experience taking on a stronger cerebral edge. The cultivar therefore behaves differently from weed that peaks almost immediately and then steadily declines.

At 19–23% THC, potency is meaningful without being defined by extreme modern laboratory numbers. Consumers with established tolerance may find the combination balanced and long lasting, while inexperienced users can still become uncomfortable if they consume too much before the delayed portion of the high develops. Dry mouth, dizziness, anxiety, short-term memory disruption, and reduced coordination remain possible with excessive THC. Waiting for the first serving to fully develop is particularly sensible with a cultivar explicitly bred for a creeper-style effect.
Medical Benefits

No controlled clinical research has evaluated Yummy itself as a treatment for a specific disease or symptom. Its combination of physical relaxation and a mood-oriented cerebral component may be appealing to some medical marijuana consumers seeking temporary relief from tension, discomfort, poor appetite, or difficulty unwinding, but those experiences should not be confused with established strain-specific medical evidence.

Research into cannabis and cannabinoids more generally suggests modest benefit for certain forms of chronic pain and has examined cannabinoids for sleep, nausea, appetite, and several neurological conditions. Results depend heavily on dose, cannabinoid composition, delivery method, and the population being studied. A seed-grown THC-rich cannabis cultivar is not chemically standardized in the way a pharmaceutical preparation is, so findings from cannabinoid studies cannot simply be assigned to Yummy.

The strain’s THC content also creates potential disadvantages. Larger doses can impair attention, memory, judgment, and coordination, while susceptible individuals may experience anxiety or dizziness. Cannabinoids can interact with some medications as well. Medical consumers should therefore use current cannabinoid testing and appropriate professional guidance rather than assuming the strain name or its relaxing reputation predicts a specific therapeutic effect.
Flavor Profile and Aroma

Sweetness forms the backbone of Yummy’s flavor. Resin Seeds specifically selected the Yumbolt parent for this quality, and Sagarmatha’s own description of Yumbolt emphasizes an exceptionally sweet flavor that remains noticeable throughout the smoking experience. That sweet foundation can resemble ripe fruit or berries rather than the artificial candy profile common in many current hybrids.

The G13 Haze male supplies the contrast. Resin Seeds highlights spice as one of the traits added by that parent, while the broader G13/Haze family brings dry herbal, earthy, woody, citrus, and incense-like possibilities into the aromatic range. Properly cured flower can therefore move from sweet fruit on the opening inhale into a drier, spicier finish, with Haze character becoming more noticeable after the initial sweetness fades.

No authoritative Resin Seeds laboratory terpene profile has been published for Yummy. Assigning exact percentages of myrcene, limonene, caryophyllene, terpinolene, or pinene would therefore be speculative. The documented breeder description is more reliable: strong Yumbolt sweetness combined with additional G13 Haze spice. Harvest conditions and curing also matter considerably. Excessive drying heat can erase brighter fruit and citrus notes, leaving a flatter mixture of wood, herbs, and earth.
Growing Information

Resin Seeds gives Yummy an indoor flowering period of 9–10 weeks. That relatively long bloom reflects its 60% sativa classification and G13 Haze ancestry but remains much more manageable than many traditional Haze plants. Indoor production is listed at approximately 400 grams per square meter under favorable conditions.

Growers should anticipate a plant with enough sativa influence to benefit from canopy control. Training before and during the early flowering stretch can help distribute branches across the available light footprint rather than allowing one or two shoots to dominate vertically. Maintaining airflow through the interior canopy becomes increasingly important as flowers gain weight, while removing unnecessary shaded growth can help direct plant energy toward well-lit bud sites.

Outdoor cultivation is scheduled for September through October according to Resin Seeds, with breeder-listed production of approximately 150–300 grams per plant. Climate therefore matters. Gardens with dry, mild autumn weather provide more flexibility than regions where cold rain arrives early. Plants expressing more of the G13 Haze side may require additional time, while Yumbolt-influenced individuals may mature somewhat more compactly.

Post-harvest patience is particularly worthwhile. Much of the cultivar’s identity lies in the contrast between sweet fruit and Haze spice, both of which can lose clarity if flower is dried aggressively. A controlled dry followed by a steady cure allows moisture within the buds to equalize while preserving more of the volatile aromatic compounds. Properly handled Yummy should smell layered rather than merely sweet, with fruit giving way to spice, herbs, and deeper earthy notes.
FAQ
What strain is Yummy?

Yummy is a sativa-dominant hybrid bred by Resin Seeds from Yumbolt × G13 Haze. The breeder selected a special Yumbolt female in 2003 and crossed it with a G13 Haze male to combine sweetness and physical relaxation with spice and a slow-building cerebral high.
Is Yummy indica or sativa?

Resin Seeds classifies the strain as 60% sativa and 40% indica. Its experience reflects both sides: a relaxing physical foundation from Yumbolt combines with a stronger cerebral component inherited from G13 Haze.
How strong is the Yummy strain?

The breeder lists THC at approximately 19–23%. That puts it in the moderately high to high-potency category, particularly because the effects can continue building after consumption instead of peaking immediately.
What does Yummy taste like?

Sweet fruit is the central flavor, supported by spice, herbs, citrus, wood, earth, and Haze-like aromatic depth. Yumbolt supplies much of the sweetness, while G13 Haze adds the spicier and more cerebral side of the cultivar.
How long does Yummy take to flower?
Resin Seeds lists approximately 9–10 weeks indoors. Outdoor harvest falls between September and October, with breeder-listed yields of about 400 g/m² indoors and 150–300 g per plant outdoors.
Final Thoughts on Yummy

Yummy has a much stronger pedigree than its playful name might suggest. Resin Seeds started with a Yumbolt female selected in 2003 rather than a generic sweet cultivar, then crossed it with G13 Haze to deliberately add spice and a slow-building cerebral dimension. That choice brought together two very different branches of cannabis history: old Humboldt-associated Yumbolt genetics and the famous G13/Haze breeding family.

The Yumbolt side is particularly significant. Sagarmatha’s cultivar carried a reputation for dense flowers, pronounced sweetness, a dreamy stone, and a first-place finish at the 2001 High Times Cannabis Cup. G13 Haze contributes Afghan and Haze ancestry along with greater mental intensity and breeding vigor. Yummy distills those influences into a 60/40 sativa-leaning hybrid with 19–23% THC and a 9–10 week flowering cycle.

For growers, the cultivar offers moderate production rather than enormous headline yields: approximately 400 g/m² indoors and 150–300 g per plant outdoors according to Resin Seeds. For consumers, flavor and effect are the more compelling reasons to seek it out. Sweet fruit gives way to spice and deeper Haze character, while comfortable physical relaxation is gradually joined by a cerebral high that can continue gaining strength after the initial inhale.

That progression gives Yummy an identity very different from contemporary candy strains whose appeal often begins and ends with sweetness. Its flavor is sweet because of Yumbolt, but its structure, spice, and creeping psychoactivity are equally important. For enthusiasts interested in Resin Seeds genetics, Humboldt-influenced cultivars, or older G13 Haze crosses, Yummy remains a well-documented hybrid with a genuine breeder history behind the name.
